x: They finished 2nd and 5th respectively in the furlong final. Youths John Kelly and Rich. Moody had a ding-dong battle in the 880 final with John just beating Rich. for 4th place on the run-in.
John Kelly put up the fastest time in the heats of the youths 880y (2:07.0) but couldn't quite repeat the performance in the final (2:10.0), a good performance nevertheless.

John Kelly won the Belgrave Youth's cross-country championship for the "Overseas Cup". He went off course after about a mile and a half and made various detours in and around the bushes surrounding Queensmere Lake but the whole field followed in his footsteps and it made no difference to the result.

This,incidentally, is 39 secs. faster than John Bicourt's winning time in the Surrey Championship over the same course, less approx. 75 yards at the finish. That surfin',hammer throwing,vodka drinking,half-miler - John Kelly was 2nd in 33:37 and Phil Smith 3rd, 13 seconds later.
LEFT: Two of our promising boys Russell Ward(1) and Alan Dunn (3). RIGHT: Youth runner, John Kelly. We went into the final fixture with an outside chance of securing a final league place of 3rd.
Tony Brooks, Richard Moody and John Kelly packed well to be our first three home and if they keep at it could be doing likewise in our future senior teams.
Coach Dave Ansell achieved a lifetime best in the shot and with his generous handicap mark of 15'3" took 1st prize from Tony Brooks and John Kelly.
The 'half' was a great race, John Phelan(Wimbledon) making the pace until John Kelly(n.s Junior) shot past, attempting a long run for home with over 500yds left.
Main points scorers have been John Kelly, Tony Brooks and Philip Gee - all first year Juniors, and Stevie White who is only a first year Youth and one of the most promising young athletes we have.
John Kelly, another versatile athlete, was 2nd in the Javelin and 880y, having led for 660y, dropped to a 10y deficit and then all but winning with a final desperate effort.

John Kelly ran an excellent 2:02.9 for the 880y, finishing 2nd to Pinfield of Mitcham. As usual he made all the early pace, leading past the bell in 60.0secs. but falling back slightly with 220y to go.

John Kelly found himself run out of the final in the half-mile during a tactical race. The first lap was taken at 61.4 and the result was a fast second lap of 59.0 odd - too fast for John,but better luck next year.
Prior to running 54.8 in the 440yds, John Kelly had finished 3rd in the Senior 880yds with 2:04.7. Match: 1.BELGRAVE H 28pts, 2.Polytechnic H 8pts.
Yet again John Kelly had a duel with Hylands (Hercules) who was this time running as a guest, and once again he was just pipped, the rest of the field way back.

Another Belgrave team win with two individual firsts from John Kelly with the unlikely combination of Javelin and 880y(report elsewhere) and another double from Tony Brooks in the two longer sprints with further places in the Javelin and Long Jump.

Jim Tappy showed some good speed by running home 3rd in the 880yds, in which John Kelly was beaten into 2nd place. Philip Gee romped both sprints with Tony Brooks giving us another 52.0 clocking in the 440yds.
The 880y promised to be an interesting race and,as in the Senior event,there was a false start as John Kelly prepared to tear away from his faster finishing rival Tony.

John Kelly was given 2:00.0 exactly in the 880yds with Adrian Major setting up his best of 2:01.0 in 4th place. Jim Johnson(LAC) won the event with an easy 1:53.3 after John Thresher had taken the first lap in 56 seconds.
Whilst Brighton took over the lead on stage 2, John Kelly put all he had into retrieving the situation for the home team, hauling us up five places and recording the fastest time of our quartet.

At present we have a very keen Youth section which will certainly improve under the training of Tom Carter and Reg Hopkins but their performances were not good enough to obtain a higher place than 14th out of the 22 teams that finished. John Kelly was our best runner with a time of 8:54.

John Kelly set off at a fiery pace which he was unable to maintain but, nevertheless, held on well to finish a creditable 9th. Good support by Poole, Curtin and Bacon - all with the makings of future first team men - and the "experienced" backing of Tony Brooks was too much for our main rivals both…
Tony Brooks (41) 46th, John Kelly (45) 31st and Richard Moody (46) 36th seen competing in the Youth's Race. Adrian Major (18) and John Martin (20) were 16th and 45th respectively in the Junior event.

The Youths C.C.Championship for the 'Overseas Cup' ended in a convincing win for John Kelly who was already the holder. The Boys race held in conjunction was won by Robert Poole in 16:26 which put him in 4th place in the overall race; quite a feat for a 14 year old.
Youth John Kelly was 2nd after running the entire race on his own, followed home three-quarters of a minute later by Phil Smith who ran extremely well to beat Derek Hurd.

John Kelly led the Youths home, with the team hitting exactly 1,000 points-- 19 fewer than their Junior friends---but this essentially track team look all set to reap the benefit of their winter's work this coming summer.

Two Juniors who are the fastest in the Club to date and who fill the bill admirably are Tony Brooks and John Kelly. THAT Charlie Walker has been kidnapped by the Noise Abatement Society! THAT John Kelly joined the City Police to get off a driving charge!

Bill Curtin was a comfortable winner of this year's Youths' championship over 2½ miles of wet going on a dank Saturday afternoon. He held off Cliff Calderwood with something in hand and both ran faster than John Kelly's winning time of 15:52 last year.

The best performance in the 'B' team was without doubt John Kelly's who during the road relay season had been running well below his best but on this occasion came up to 136th which should encourage him for future races during the winter.
There were ten starters in the Junior event and John Kelly, runner up to Adrian Major last year, must have been hoping to step up a place before he joins the Senior ranks.

A word of praise for Charlie Walker who is again showing his true form - this enabled him to take first prize in the handicap with John Stow, an up and coming young member second and John Kelly third.

Any one of John Boardman, Douglas Jardine, John Kelly, Lionel Mann (no '20' the week before!) could get under 1 minute 55 secs. and then improve, while the "veteran" track captain isn't giving up yet!

I think we could at last have some strength in depth in the future in what has been our "Cinderella" event since the retirement of Dave Cocks; through such competitors as Mel Ford (around 1-56 relay), John Boardman, John Kelly and Doug Jardine.

A hundred yards back were Black, Rimmer and Smith, and 150 yards further behind was John Kelly---with Laurie O'Hara hard on his heels. Laurie must have covered that first lap a good 8 to 10 seconds faster than the leaders!.

On the other hand, Tony Fairclough was run off his feet and was heard to be pining for Parliament Hill with mutterings of "Wait 'till the Southern". Charlie Dabbs and John Kelly supported well and deserved their bronze medals---but that big 'IF' still remains.
We also Have John Boardman, Mel Ford and another junior, John Stowe, under the 2 minute barrier and Colin Pearson and John Kelly should also be shortly.
But John Kelly was the man to upset the form book - making a further jump towards the big-time with 28th place, just 8s. behind our English international steeplechaser John Bicourt.
The race was also something of a City of London Police convention, with our own John Kelly and David Davies in the field, together with policeman Wilde, 36th in 46m. 41s.

We might have expected John Kelly to head our challenge, but John had come on from ammorning run over 2,000m. as part of the Lord Mayor's Show, and finished back in 123rd place - Bob James' 72nd taking the honours.

Guy Monnet again showed up well, in fifth place, but John Kelly's 11th place in 46m. 6s. measured up best against Bill Lucas' yardstick, while veteran Charlie Manning pipped Guy for the third handicap spot.

It could be, at the same time, that Guy Monnet will produce an even more considerable breakthrough in coming weeks than he has already this winter, while Colin Pearson, John Kelly and Bob James are all threatening to break out of the second team ranks into the first team before long.

In his first ten-miler of the winter, he showed that he was good for the distance, pushing Lionel from start to finish, and being squeezed into second place by a mere five seconds. John Kelly ran himself into a place in the Southern team, and was a deserving winner of the handicap.
A different Guy might have been seen, however, had it not been for a poisoned tooth. John Kelly was rewarded for his recent improvement with a first run in the Southern.
They have numerous runners to back them up notably JOHN BOARDMAN BILL CURTIN, DOUGLAS JARDINE, JOHN KELLY, and LIONEL MANN - training for a fast finishing marathon.

After the courageous starter called everyone back for a false start they were away and streaking to the front in a short lived bid for glory was John Kelly but as the race progressed it was clear that Peter Carton would once again comfortably lead our team home.

Off to settle in Canada are JOHN and JILL KELLY and we wish them good luck and success in their new home. John joined us as a Youth from Battersea County School and since then has represented us over all distances up to 10 miles.
And into the centre amongst the delicately stepping lady friends and wives would troop the stomping John Martin or John Kelly with all the finesse of a couple of pampas bulls.
